# Lionel Fairlie

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P34](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0034)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** old pagan  <sub>[v5 c16 P37](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0037)</sub>

## Appearance

Lionel Fairlie is described as a somewhat handsome figure with a tall, pale forehead, a long red beard across his broad chest, and a thick mane of red hair untouched by grey despite his age. His intense blue eyes reflect the wildness of his youth, and he possesses a large frame with massive hands.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P35](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0035), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002)_

## Personality

Lionel is loud, self-satisfied, temperamental, and straightforward, never hiding his opinions or intentions from anyone. Possessing sharp intellect and extensive reading, he appreciates good sermons for their mental stimulation, though he holds no religious faith and is considered an outright pagan. Depending on his mood, he can be either exceptionally frightening or exceedingly charming, engaging in loud merriment and demonstrating a strong, stubborn will. He values spirit in women and disdains excessive submissiveness, often laughing off others' antipathy toward him.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030), [v5 c16 P32](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0032), [v5 c16 P34](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0034), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019), [v5 c26 P21](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0021), [v5 c32 P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002), [v5 c32 P8](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0008)_

- Marry Harriet Ainslie  <sub>[v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)</sub>
- Obtain Clementine Ainslie's release of Harriet's vow  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)</sub>

## History

In his youth, Lionel Fairlie spent two years courting Harriet Ainslie, but after a foolish disagreement, he impulsively married Dinah Coyle in a fit of temper. He held contempt for Dinah's weak-willed docility and crushed what little resolve she had, though she bore her submissive life without public complaint until her death ten years later. After feeling cheated over a cow deal by a church session member, Lionel ceased attending church for twenty years, insisting his late wife contribute no more than a single penny during her visits. Following a visit from young Grace Ashdown, he resumed church attendance on the first Sunday of November, making a public stir by teasing Mr. Ashdown about his deceased wife's health and commending his sermon. Entranced upon seeing Harriet Ainslie at church after two decades, he openly resumed his courtship of her. He later pursued Clementine Ainslie to Fern Hollow to obtain her consent to release Harriet from a personal vow, successfully clearing the path for his upcoming marriage.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P36](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0036), [v5 c16 P39](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0039), [v5 c17 P0](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0000), [v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001), [v5 c17 P3](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0003), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019), [v5 c32 P0](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0000), [v5 c32 P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P13](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0013)_

- Courted Harriet Ainslie in his youth before breaking up after a disagreement

> The thoughts within your father's mind surpass what his facial expression reveals. However, he made a single self-contradiction—inform him that he contradicted himself.  <sub>[v5 c17 P3](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0003)</sub>
